definitions.explanation: A type of blood cell that is part of the immune system, responsible for fighting infections and foreign substances in the body.

examples.japanese: {白血球|はっけっきゅう}の{数|かず}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: The white blood cell count is high.

examples.japanese: {白血球|はっけっきゅう}は{体|からだ}を{感染|かんせん}から{守|まも}る。
examples.english: White blood cells protect the body from infection.

examples.japanese: {血液|けつえき}{検査|けんさ}で{白血球|はっけっきゅう}の{値|あたい}が{低|ひく}いことが{分|わ}かった。
examples.english: A blood test revealed that my white blood cell count was low.

notes:
Composed of {白|はく} (white), {血|けつ} (blood), and {球|きゅう} (ball, sphere). Abbreviated as WBC in medical contexts. White blood cells are a key part of the immune system, and their count is a standard item on blood test results.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {白血球|はっけっきゅう}の{数|かず}: white blood cell count
- {白血球|はっけっきゅう}が{増|ふ}える: white blood cell count increases
- {白血球|はっけっきゅう}が{減|へ}る: white blood cell count decreases

RELATED TERMS:
- {赤血球|せっけっきゅう}: red blood cell
- {血小板|けっしょうばん}: platelet
- {白血病|はっけつびょう}: leukemia — a cancer of the blood involving abnormal white blood cells
